Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Subject: Executive Recap: Redwood Inference discussion — AuroraMed next steps

Hi Nina and Tom,

Thanks again for taking time today — really appreciated the candid discussion. Per our ask, below is a short executive recap for your leadership and procurement teams capturing outcomes, risks, and suggested next steps. Please let me know if you want any edits before I share this with our account exec and solutions engineering.

Key business drivers (what you told us):
- Reduce average documentation-processing latency from 4.2s to <1s per request for core claims workflows (goal: improve adjudication throughput by ~30%).
- Replace brittle on-prem rule parsing stack to reduce maintenance overhead and eliminate frequent outages during batch runs.
- Ensure PHI handling and auditability to satisfy upcoming payer audits (Q2 2027).

Primary risks & open questions:
1) Data residency / ingestion: you will confirm whether redacted extracts are OK or full PHI is required for model tuning.
2) SLA expectations: AuroraMed requires 99.95% availability for the production path — we can support via Dedicated reservations but need procurement sign-off on costs.
3) Integration velocity: IT platform is on Azure but you also use a private on-prem data lake; need to agree on network/peering approach for Private deployment.

Proposed outcomes & next steps:
- Redwood will deliver a draft mutual action plan (MAP) and updated pricing proposal by Monday 11/23 (attached: mutual_action_plan.docx, redwood_pricing_proposal_v2.pdf).
- Technical deep-dive (Solutions Eng + AuroraMed infra) to be scheduled w/in next 7 business days to scope network and onboarding tasks.
- Procurement path: Tom, please confirm whether AuroraMed prefers a PO + SOW or a platform subscription with MSAs/ordering docs — Redwood can accept either.
- Security artifacts: attached SOC2 summary and SOC2 Kit link; we can provide additional evidence and a short on-site compliance review if required.

Escalation items for execs:
- If AuroraMed requires full PHI for model tuning, that will change the deployment model and timeline; we should escalate to security & legal for a scoped DPA amendment and potential private-hosting pricing.
- If a 99.95% SLA is mandatory from day 1, we will need an upfront Dedicated reservation and associated commit.

Next meeting proposal:
- Technical kickoff (Solutions Eng + Infra): Thu 11/26 10:00–11:00 PT
- Executive checklist (finalize MAP + procurement path): Tue 12/1 9:00–9:30 PT

Thanks — attaching the MAP, updated pricing, and SOC2 summary for your review.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.docx; redwood_pricing_proposal_v2.pdf; soc2_summary.xlsx
From: nina.patel@auroramed.com

Subject: Re: Executive Recap: Redwood Inference discussion — AuroraMed next steps

Laura — thanks for the concise recap. This captures the conversation well. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We will likely be able to provide de-identified datasets for initial tuning but the business is asking whether there is a path to use PHI later in a controlled way (we need the legal/security view).
- Procurement note: AuroraMed prefers PO + SOW for any vendor work. Our standard procurement timeline is ~3–4 weeks once legal has the final SOW.
- SLA: 99.95% is preferred but we may accept a staged SLA (e.g., 99.5% during pilot, 99.95% in production) if cost delta is material.

Action items for Redwood:
1) Please highlight cost delta between pilot and production SLA in the pricing doc.
2) Provide a short statement on how Redwood handles PHI in Private deployments and any available customer references for regulated workloads.
3) Book the technical deep-dive (we prefer next Wed or Thu morning ET).

I'll loop Tom on procurement specifics; he'll confirm PO/SOW contacts.

-Nina
